lines: A phase modulation effect for any two audio signals: the carrier is written into a delay line and the modulator moves the point it is read back from, which gives the harmonics of DX-style FM
Sets how far the modulator moves the read point, reaching 50 samples per volt of modulator at full travel; more of it adds higher harmonics
Attenuates and inverts the DEPTH CV input, from -1 at full counter-clockwise through 0 at noon to +1 at full clockwise, before it is added to the FM DEPTH knob
The carrier, which is the signal written into the delay line and read back modulated
The modulator, whose voltage moves the read point and so modulates the phase of the carrier
Modulates the FM depth: the voltage is divided by 5, scaled by the attenuverter and added to the FM DEPTH knob, and the total is clamped to the knob's own 0 to 1 range
The modulated carrier, at as many channels as the wider of IN and MOD IN
Note — the read point starts 5ms behind the write point, so the output lags the input by 5ms with no modulation applied
Note — depth changes are smoothed, each sample moving a thousandth of the way to the new value, so turning FM DEPTH or moving its CV arrives over a few tens of milliseconds

FMtool.notes: The README calls the trimpot the Depth CV knob and the jack the Depth CV in port; the panel prints DEPTH CV once between them. The maker's tooltip for the trimpot is CV Depth Attenuation, and the parameter's range of -1 to +1 makes it an attenuverter rather than an attenuator. A 4096-sample buffer at FMtool.cpp:27 limits how far the modulation can push the read point before it wraps.

lines: Turns any audio input into a pulse wave whose width you set and modulate, by comparing the input against a threshold or by subtracting a delayed copy of it from itself
Sets the pulse width, from 0.01 to 0.99 of a cycle; 0.5 gives a square wave with odd harmonics only, and moving away from it brings in even harmonics
Sets the frequency of the internal LFO that modulates the width, from 0.1Hz to 20Hz; with a cable in PWM CV the LFO is not used and this knob changes nothing you can hear
Scales how far the width is modulated, by the internal LFO when PWM CV is empty and by the PWM CV voltage when it is patched; the swing is proportional to the PULSE WIDTH setting
Crossfades between the dry input and the pulse; at 100% only the pulse is heard
The audio input that is turned into a pulse wave
Tracks the pitch of the input so the delay stays the same fraction of a cycle at every note; in comparator mode nothing in the output depends on it
Modulates the pulse width and replaces the internal LFO for as long as a cable is in it; ±5V gives the full swing set by PWM DEPTH
The pulse, crossfaded with the dry input by MIX, at as many channels as the wider of IN and V/OCT
Note — the module comes up in comparator mode, and delay mode is chosen from the panel menu
Note — in delay mode patch V/OCT, or the delay is computed as though the input were C4 at 261.63Hz and the width will be wrong at every other pitch
Note — the width is clamped to between 0.01 and 0.99 of a cycle, so neither the knob nor the modulation can close the pulse completely
Menu — Comparator Mode — the output swings to 5V whenever the input is above a threshold set by PULSE WIDTH and to -5V otherwise, which works with any input and needs no V/OCT
Menu — Delay Mode — subtracts a delayed copy of the input from itself, the delay being the pulse width as a fraction of one cycle, which suits sawtooth inputs and keeps more of the input's character

PWM.notes: The mode is a parameter, MODE_PARAM, but it has no widget on the panel, so it can only be set from the panel menu and no click can reach it for help. Its default of 1 is comparator mode. Both modes pass the result through a one-pole lowpass at 19000Hz. In delay mode a pitch change of a semitone or more starts a 0.05 second crossfade onto a second delay line, and smaller changes glide the delay time instead, which is what the README describes as tracking legato and vibrato. The README says the PWM rate knob is unused when PWM CV is connected; the code still advances the LFO, it simply discards its value, so the effect is as the README says. Comparator mode also multiplies the pulse by an envelope taken from the rectified input, so silence at the input gives silence rather than a DC offset.
